{{Biathlon at the 2026 Winter Olympics}}
The '''women's individual''' competition of the [[Biathlon at the 2026 Winter Olympics|2026 Winter Olympics]] was held on 11 February,<!-- 2026--> at the [[South Tyrol Arena|Anterselva Biathlon Arena]] in [[Rasen-Antholz]].<ref name="schedule">{{cite web|url=https://www.biathlonworld.com/calendar?SeasonId=2526&CupLevel=1&EventId=BT2526SWRLOG__|title=2026 Olympic Games – Antholz-Anterselva|publisher=[[International Biathlon Union|IBU]]|access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> [[Julia Simon (biathlete)|Julia Simon]] of France won the event, her teammate [[Lou Jeanmonnot]] was second, and [[Lora Hristova]] of Bulgaria third.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260219-french-biathlete-simon-finds-the-golden-touch-at-2026-winter-olympics|title=French biathlete Julia Simon finds golden touch at 2026 Winter Olympics|publisher=Radio France Internationale|accessdate=27 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cddn09qer22o|title=Simon wins gold after credit card fraud conviction|publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=27 February 2026}}</ref> For all of them, these were their first individual Olympic medals.

==Background==
The 2022 champion, [[Denise Herrmann-Wick|Denise Herrmann]], retired from competitions, as did the silver medalist [[Anaïs Chevalier-Bouchet]] and the bronze medalist [[Marte Olsbu Røiseland]]. Prior to the Olympics, [[Lou Jeanmonnot]] was leading the total as well as individual standings of the [[2025–26 Biathlon World Cup]]. [[Julia Simon (biathlete)|Julia Simon]] was the [[Biathlon World Championships 2025 – Women's individual|2025 World champion]].
